content: To create a microchaptered page, follow these detailed steps: Searching for the Page You Want to Create 1. Begin by searching for the disease name of the page you intend to create. 2. Additionally, search for synonyms or alternative names of the disease to avoid duplicating content. 3. If the page already exists but is not microchaptered, you may create a new microchaptered page for the disease. Afterward, reorganize the existing content into the microchaptered format. 4. Only proceed with microchaptering if the page exceeds one-and-a-half pages in length and contains sufficient content (or will have enough content) to justify dividing it into microchapters. 5. To reorganize the content, follow the instructions for creating a microchapter template. Copy and paste the existing information into the standardized microchapter structure. Creating a Microchapter Template 1. If the disease page does not exist, you will need to create a new microchaptered page. 2. Navigate to the WikiDoc Disease Microchapter Template, which can be found on the home page under the Advanced Editing section. 3. Click on the Edit tab and copy all the text from the edit box. 4. In the main WikiDoc search box, type Template:[Disease Name] (e.g., Template:Jaundice) without quotation marks. 5. Click on the option to Create the page Template:[Disease Name] on this Wiki. 6. Paste the copied microchapter template information into the edit box. 7. At the top of the edit box, you will see two blank fields: The top field, marked with binocular icons, should contain type page name here. The bottom field, marked with red arrows, should contain the name of the disease page you are creating. 8. Click the red arrows on the right side of the bottom field repeatedly until the disease name is inserted into all the microchapter navigation boxes. 9. Remove any cells in the template that are not relevant to the disease you are working on. 10. Save your changes at the bottom of the edit box. 11. You now have a microchapter navigation template that can be used for all subsequent microchapter pages you create. Creating the Microchaptered Home Page 1. Search for the disease name in the WikiDoc search box. 2. If no page exists, click on the option to Create the page [Disease Name] on this Wiki. 3. In the edit box, type `{{[Disease Name]}}` (e.g., `{{Jaundice}}`). 4. Save your changes at the bottom of the edit box. The main page will now display the microchapter navigation template on the right side. 5. Use the microchapter template for all subsequent microchapter pages by typing `{{[Disease Name]}}` into the edit box of each page. 6. The home page should also include links to the individual microchapter pages in the correct order. To do this: Use the format `==[Link]==` in the edit box. On the left side of the vertical line, include the link to the page. On the right side, specify how the link should appear on the page. For example, the link might appear as Historical Perspective on the main page. 7. Copy the template information from the edit box and paste it into the home page of the microchaptered page you are creating. 8. Use the search-and-replace function to replace Type page name here with the name of the disease (e.g., Jaundice). 9. Remove any links that are not relevant to the disease. 10. For additional guidance on creating links, refer to the relevant instructions. 11. Note that while microchapter pages use lowercase headings, the links on the home page may appear differently. Maintain consistency in capitalization and nomenclature by referencing the provided examples. Creating Individual Pages Within a Microchaptered Page 1. The home page will display the microchapter navigation template on the right side of the screen, with the headings of the microchapters in the center. These headings will link to the corresponding microchapter pages. 2. To practice navigating a microchaptered page, refer to the provided example. 3. As you create new microchapter pages, add links to them on the home page. 4. To create a new microchapter page, click on the relevant section within the microchapter navigation template on the home page. 5. Select the option to Create the page [Microchapter Name] on this Wiki. 6. Use the appropriate template listed on the main page to create the new microchapter page.g., `{{Jaundice}}`) is included on each microchapter page. References and Sources 1. If the content for the page is derived from general sources, such as textbooks or websites, list them under a heading titled Sources at the bottom of the page. 2. If the content is based on journal articles or other scholarly articles, list them under a heading titled References at the bottom of the page. 3. For detailed instructions on how to insert references, refer to the relevant guidelines.
